evals.prompt: /firststone — new project Portal for client Acme. Home repo and one new Python app repo on GitHub under the acme-team org; gh is authenticated with admin rights. Two team members, one client contact.
evals.expected_output: The agent completes the interview, shows a plan and writes nothing before the user confirms. It then creates portal-knowledge with AGENTS.md (pointers only), docs/agents/workflow.md, docs/agents/team.md and .gitignore, pushes the first commit to main and creates the retro label. In the app repo it works on firststone/setup, adds CONTRIBUTING.md, .pre-commit-config.yaml and a GitHub Actions workflow, opens a PR, and protects main with PR required and zero approvals. It opens the setup issue and ends by telling the user to run /setup-matt-pocock-skills and then /ask-matt. Fixed rules: every written file has content, nothing in the app repo mentions the home repo or its tracker, and the meeting-update format names no tool.

evals.prompt: /firststone — project Billing for client Northwind. The client already created the app repo on GitHub; it contains a CONTRIBUTING.md, a .github/pull_request_template.md and a Node package.json with lint and test scripts. I cloned it at ~/repos/northwind/billing-api.
evals.expected_output: The agent leaves CONTRIBUTING.md, the PR template and package.json byte-identical and reports them as overlaps in the plan and the summary. Because the repo is the client's, it writes no husky files: adopting husky is one open step naming the two package.json edits and the two hook files. Whatever it does add goes on the firststone/setup branch through a PR, never to main; a branch that adds nothing is not pushed. Protection of main defers to the client's own review rule. Fixed rules: every written file has content, nothing in the app repo mentions the home repo or its tracker.

evals.prompt: /firststone — project Atlas for client Contoso, one new app repo on GitHub. We have not chosen the stack yet.
evals.expected_output: The agent writes CONTRIBUTING.md without a local-checks section, writes no hook and no CI file, and adds the open step 'rerun /firststone once the stack is chosen' to the setup issue. Fixed rules: every written file has content, nothing in the app repo mentions the home repo or its tracker.

evals.prompt: /firststone — project Portal for client Acme. Home repo on our GitHub org; the client's app repo is on Bitbucket, Python, already created. PRs are opened from the Bitbucket site and CI runs on the client's Jenkins.
evals.expected_output: In the app repo the agent uses plain Git only: clone, firststone/setup branch, commit, push. It writes CONTRIBUTING.md and the pre-commit configuration and no CI file. Opening the PR, protecting main and configuring CI are open steps on the setup issue; the agent does not invent Bitbucket menu paths. The user's two lines about PRs and CI appear under Repo notes in workflow.md. Fixed rules: every written file has content, nothing in the app repo mentions the home repo or its tracker.

evals.prompt: /firststone — project Portal for client Acme on GitHub, one Python app repo. The team uses Claude Code. Only firststone is installed on this machine.
evals.expected_output: The agent lists in the plan the skills it will commit into the home repo, installs them from the home repo with npx skills add mattpocock/skills --skill <the engineering set> --agent claude-code --copy -y, and commits the skill folders together with skills-lock.json. It installs nothing globally, and the setup checklist has no line asking teammates to install skills. workflow.md says skills are updated at the weekly retro with npx skills update -p through a PR.

evals.prompt: /firststone — project Portal for client Acme on GitHub, one Python app repo we own. We need to move fast: I must be able to merge my own PRs when my colleague is busy.
evals.expected_output: The agent protects main with PR required and zero required approvals. workflow.md and CONTRIBUTING.md state that review is requested from the other person, that the author may merge without waiting after /code-review and green checks, and that the PR then carries a 'Merged without review: <reason>' line.
